glance_takeaway: This is a blameless post-incident review of INC-1194, an outage of the Ledgerline Invoicing API on June 24, 2026. The main message is that there was no single root cause: a rewritten search query hit two dormant weaknesses (vacuum debt and jitterless retries), turning a one-endpoint regression into a platform-wide partial outage lasting 4h17m with a 31.2% peak error rate, 2,312 orgs affected (24.4%), and roughly $41,300 in SLA credits. Rollback was impossible; a feature flag stopped it, and three P0 fixes land Q3 2026.

strengths: Near-complete fact coverage: 15 of 16 facts conveyed, zero distortions or contradictions, with timestamps and quantities matching ground truth exactly.

The causal structure is the page's spine: one slide per cause with consistent color tags, then a combination slide whose counterfactual chips ('No bloat -> ...', 'No retry storm -> ...') directly render T1's remove-any-leg logic.
All SVG encodings are proportionally honest (verified pixel scales on the timeline, dead-tuple bar, scan-time-vs-timeout bar, pool-demand bar, and 68-minute diagnosis bar).
One-line glosses for every DB-specific mechanism (index, dead tuples, pgbouncer pool) exactly as the brief's audience requires.
Recap slide compresses the story into five lines with deep links back to evidence slides - directly serves the 'brief your own team' reading goal.
Uncertainty markers from the source (approx, ~, estimated) are preserved throughout; blameless tone is explicit ('given what responders could see, the network theory was reasonable').
weaknesses: F3 (endpoint latency impact: p50 85ms->2.9s, p99 420ms->28.4s) is entirely absent - the customer-experienced latency story is told only via query time and error rate.
T2 (the 68-minute misdiagnosis) is invisible at a glance - nothing above the fold hints at detection lag, so a skimmer misses one of four required takeaways.
Wayfinding depends on hover-only rail tooltips (suppressed on mobile) and there is no upfront table of contents; a reader hunting for one number must scroll or already know the recap slide has links.
Mandatory scroll-snap paging can fight readers who want to compare adjacent slides or skim at their own pace.
Individual remediation owners (Priya N., Marcus T., Dana K.) are dropped in favor of team names, weakening the 'named owners' accountability signal.
evaluator_notes: Accuracy = 10 * 15 conveyed / 16 facts = 9.4 (0 distorted, 0 contradicted). Overall = 0.35*9.4 + 0.30*7.0 + 0.15*8.0 + 0.10*7.5 + 0.10*8.5 = 8.2. Glance pass: cover lands T1 strongly, T3 in compressed form, T4 partially (count + quarter + 'blameless' kicker); T2 absent above the fold -> 7.0. The high overall is earned almost entirely by the fact audit and verified-honest charting; the page's main real gaps are the missing endpoint-latency numbers and glance-invisibility of the detection-lag takeaway.
